_meta.method: Merged from two research passes: (A) Wikipedia, provincial tourism portals, Thiền phái Trúc Lâm websites, phatgiao.org.vn, langmai.org — Trúc Lâm head/training centers and Lâm Tế / Liễu Quán heritage temples in Huế and Saigon; (B) earlier pass on additional Trúc Lâm provincial monasteries and major Lâm Tế pagodas (Quán Sứ, Giác Lâm, Phước Hải, Vĩnh Tràng).
_meta.coverageEstimate: Trúc Lâm head-network largely covered (≈40% of all thiền viện), plus the major Lâm Tế / Liễu Quán Huế temples and Plum Village's Vietnamese root. Many smaller provincial Lâm Tế pagodas omitted.
knownGaps: Smaller Trúc Lâm thiền viện in less-prominent provinces
Hundreds of village-level Lâm Tế pagodas without standalone English-language sources
Most Quán Âm / Pure Land-leaning pagodas (out of scope: not primarily Zen practice)

batch29.scope: Item-level authoritative evidence check for Tổ đình Từ Hiếu and Vĩnh Tràng Pagoda from practice evidence review Batch 29
batch29.interpretation: Official temple/community or national tourism pages support each named entity and location. Current administrative naming for Vĩnh Tràng reflects the 2025 Tiền Giang–Đồng Tháp provincial merger, while the tourism profile retains historical labels. Heritage and institutional evidence do not establish recurring public Zen practice; missing schedule evidence is uncertainty, not evidence of misconduct or inactivity.

places.name: Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Yên Tử
places.address: Thôn Nam Mẫu, xã Thượng Yên Công, thành phố Uông Bí, tỉnh Quảng Ninh, Việt Nam
places.notes: Official provincial Buddhist Sangha information identifies the monastery as a place for meditation instruction for monastics, Buddhists, and other interested people, alongside tourism and pilgrimage functions; recurring public session details were not established.

places.name: Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Đà Lạt
places.address: Đường Trúc Lâm Yên Tử, phường 3, thành phố Đà Lạt, tỉnh Lâm Đồng, Việt Nam
places.notes: Lâm Đồng provincial tourism authority identifies the Trúc Lâm monastery, its resident monastic community, and daily monastic training, and treats it as a visitor destination. Institutional practice and visitor access are evidenced; no lay public timetable is published. Checked 2026-10-08.

places.name: Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Tây Thiên
places.address: Xã Đại Đình, huyện Tam Đảo, tỉnh Vĩnh Phúc, Việt Nam
places.notes: Official Phú Thọ tourism portal identifies the Trúc Lâm monastery in the Tây Thiên scenic complex and its pilgrimage/visitor role; no recurring public Zen timetable was found.

places.name: Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Bạch Mã
places.address: Hồ Truồi, Huế City, Vietnam
places.notes: Trúc Lâm Yên Tử monastery at Hồ Truồi, Huế. The Huế tourism department identifies it as the fourth monastery in the Trúc Lâm Yên Tử school and says it was completed in 2008 for worship and monastic practice; the page also describes pilgrim visits. No current public meditation schedule or access policy was found. Present as a monastery and pilgrimage venue, not as a confirmed drop-in practice group.

places.name: Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Phụng Hoàng
places.address: Khu phố 7, phường 3, thành phố Đà Lạt, tỉnh Lâm Đồng, Việt Nam
places.notes: Lâm Đồng provincial tourism authority describes Trúc Lâm monastery on Phụng Hoàng hill, with resident monastics and daily monastic training. The evidence points to the already listed Trúc Lâm Đà Lạt monastery, with Phụng Hoàng as the hill name; a separate institution under this name is not established. Visitor access is described; no lay public timetable is published. Checked 2026-10-08.

places.name: Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Phương Nam
places.address: Ấp Nhơn Mỹ, xã Mỹ Khánh, huyện Phong Điền, thành phố Cần Thơ, Việt Nam
places.notes: Trúc Lâm-named Buddhist monastery and pilgrimage venue in Cần Thơ. The city tourism portal gives the historic address at Lộ Vòng Cung, Mỹ Khánh, Phong Điền and describes worship visits; its ward/district labels predate administrative changes. A current directory associates management with the Cần Thơ Buddhist Sangha and gives An Bình ward, but no monastery-run page or public Zen schedule was found. Verify the current address before travel; do not infer recurring public meditation.

places.name: Thiền viện Thường Chiếu
places.lineage: Trúc Lâm (Thiền phái Trúc Lâm Việt Nam)
places.address: Số 001, tổ 23, ấp 1C, xã Phước Thái, huyện Long Thành, tỉnh Đồng Nai, Việt Nam
places.notes: Current local-government records identify this Phước Thái monastery; Buddhist community reporting identifies it with Thích Thanh Từ’s Trúc Lâm lineage. No current public visitor schedule was verified (checked 2026-10-08).

places.name: Thiền viện Linh Chiếu
places.address: Xã Phước Thái, huyện Long Thành, tỉnh Đồng Nai, Việt Nam
places.notes: Nuns’ monastery in the Trúc Lâm Vietnamese Zen tradition at Phước Thái, Đồng Nai. A Vietnam Buddhist Sangha report records a July 2026 visit and identifies its abbess as a board member of the Trúc Lâm Vietnamese Zen school; a Trúc Lâm tradition page records the monastery’s 1980 founding under Thích Thanh Từ. The provincial Sangha documented it as a monastic summer retreat venue in 2023. No current public visitor policy or recurring public sitting schedule was found.

places.name: Thiền viện Viên Chiếu
places.address: Xã Phước Bình, huyện Long Thành, tỉnh Đồng Nai, Việt Nam
places.notes: Local-government records identify this Long Thành nunnery, and historical Buddhist scholarship places it in Thích Thanh Từ’s Trúc Lâm tradition. Public sources disagree on the precise commune, so confirm before visiting (checked 2026-10-08).

places.name: Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Trí Đức
places.address: Xã An Phước, huyện Long Thành, tỉnh Đồng Nai, Việt Nam
places.notes: Trúc Lâm monastery on 10.5 hectares in An Phước, Long Thành; construction began 2009 and was inaugurated in 2011 with Hòa thượng Thích Thanh Từ presiding over the ceremony.

places.name: Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Long Đức
places.address: Khu 15, huyện Long Thành, tỉnh Đồng Nai, Việt Nam
places.notes: Trúc Lâm Long Đức in Long Thành was offered as a 2-hectare temple complex to Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Trí Đức; Hòa thượng Thích Nhật Quang, head of the Trúc Lâm Việt Nam board, serves as trụ trì.

places.name: Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Hậu Giang
places.notes: Trúc Lâm-named Buddhist monastery in the former Hậu Giang area, now within Cần Thơ municipality. The former provincial tourism office describes it as a Buddhist community center and visitor destination with listed hours of 07:00–18:00 and a campus including lecture hall, monastic quarters, and guest facilities. Its page conflicts on ward naming (Long Bình vs. Vĩnh Tường) and predates the municipal merger; its current address and map position need local verification. No public Zen teaching schedule was found.

places.name: Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Tây Ninh
places.address: Phường Gia Lộc, thị xã Trảng Bàng, tỉnh Tây Ninh, Việt Nam
places.notes: Giác Ngộ, the Vietnamese Buddhist Sangha news portal, reports a 2026 ceremony at the monastery and identifies its abbot and Trúc Lâm lineage. This is institutional/event evidence; the article describes construction of the main hall and does not establish a recurring public practice schedule or visitor timetable. Checked 2026-10-08.

places.name: Tổ đình Từ Hiếu
places.lineage: Thiền tông (Lâm Tế / Liễu Quán; root temple of Plum Village / Làng Mai)
places.address: Dương Xuân Thượng III, phường Thủy Xuân, thành phố Huế, Việt Nam
places.notes: Plum Village's item-specific official Tổ đình Từ Hiếu page identifies the Huế temple as its Vietnamese root temple, with an adjacent official contact page. Its address retains the stable Dương Xuân Thượng III / Thủy Xuân locality; Huế became a centrally administered city on 2025-01-01 (Government of Vietnam, https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/nghi-quyet-so-175-2024-qh15-thanh-lap-thanh-pho-hue-truc-thuoc-trung-uong-119241205102339073.htm). This supports institutional identity and heritage context, not a published recurring public practice timetable. Checked 2026-10-08.

places.name: Chùa Quốc Ân
places.lineage: Lâm Tế (Nguyên Thiều lineage, early Lâm Tế tổ đình in Huế)
places.notes: Historic Lâm Tế ancestral temple in Huế. The city portal’s 2025 profile identifies Zen master Nguyên Thiều as founder, reports that the site was established around 1680 and named Quốc Ân in 1689, and identifies it as an early Lâm Tế ancestral site. No current temple-run public practice schedule was found; list as a historical Zen temple, not a verified recurring sitting group. Its current street address should be verified locally.

places.name: Chùa Báo Quốc
places.lineage: Thiền/Zen (historical connection; school unverified by current source)
places.address: Đồi Hàm Long, đường Bảo Quốc, Phường Đúc ward, Huế City, Vietnam
places.notes: Historic Huế Buddhist temple. A current heritage profile lists 17 Bảo Quốc Street in Thuận Hóa ward, describes it as a Bắc Tông ancestral temple founded in the late 17th century by Zen master Giác Phong, and gives visitor hours of 07:00–17:00; the profile is not temple-run. A separate government reference uses Phường Đúc, so the current ward designation is uncertain. No current public Chan schedule was found. Describe its Zen connection as historical and visitor access as temple visitation.

places.name: Chùa Từ Đàm
places.lineage: Lâm Tế (modern central Việt Nam Mahāyāna / Liễu Quán tradition)
places.address: Số 1 đường Sư Liễu Quán, phường Trường An, thành phố Huế, tỉnh Thừa Thiên Huế, Việt Nam
places.notes: Huế tourism authority identifies Từ Đàm as a historic Buddhist center and visitor destination. This is heritage/visitor evidence; no recurring public practice timetable was confirmed. Checked 2026-10-08.

places.name: Chùa Long Sơn
places.lineage: Lâm Tế (Đằng Long Tự, Lâm Tế đời 39)
places.address: Số 22 đường 23 Tháng 10, phường Phương Sơn, thành phố Nha Trang, tỉnh Khánh Hòa, Việt Nam
places.notes: Provincial head temple and seat of the Buddhist Sangha in Khánh Hòa; founded by a Lâm Tế lineage master (Ngộ Trí / Ngộ Chí), later rebuilt at the foot of Trại Thủy hill and hosting a large seated Buddha.

places.name: Chùa Vĩnh Nghiêm (Bắc Giang)
places.lineage: Trúc Lâm (historic center) with later Lâm Tế connections
places.address: Thôn Quốc Khánh, xã Trí Yên, huyện Yên Dũng, tỉnh Bắc Giang, Việt Nam
places.notes: Famous Đức La / Vĩnh Nghiêm temple at the confluence of the Thương and Lục Nam rivers; medieval center of the Trúc Lâm school where Trần Nhân Tông and Pháp Loa taught, now recognized as a national special relic with UNESCO-listed woodblock canon.

places.name: Chùa Vĩnh Nghiêm (Sài Gòn)
places.lineage: Bắc Tông / Trúc Lâm–Lâm Tế tradition (modeled on Vĩnh Nghiêm Bắc Giang)
places.address: Số 339 Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, phường 7, quận 3, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
places.notes: Vietnam National Authority of Tourism identifies the Ho Chi Minh City temple at 339 Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa and describes its Buddhist institutional history and architecture. This is institutional/heritage and visitor evidence; the source does not establish a recurring public practice schedule. Checked 2026-10-08.

places.address: Tân Phước District, Tiền Giang
places.notes: Official Đồng Tháp tourism portal identifies site and location as a visitor destination; it does not establish a recurring public practice schedule.

places.address: Cự Khối, Long Biên, Hanoi
places.notes: Monastery website is the institutional source for its identity and announcements. General institutional or retreat activity does not establish recurring open public practice without an explicit schedule.

places.address: Hàm Rồng Mountain, Thanh Hóa
places.notes: Monastery website is the institutional source for its identity and announcements; reviewed evidence did not establish a recurring public Zen schedule.

places.address: Sông Lô, Vĩnh Phúc

places.name: Diệu Trạm Monastery
places.lineage: Vietnamese Thiền (Plum Village — Thich Nhat Hanh tradition; sister to Từ Hiếu)
places.address: Thủy Xuân, Huế, Thừa Thiên-Huế
places.notes: Plum Village monastic practice centre for nuns in Huế and sister monastery of Từ Hiếu. The official Làng Mai site confirms the community; no regular public visitor schedule was found.

places.name: Giác Lâm Pagoda
places.address: 565 Lạc Long Quân, Hồ Chí Minh City, Vietnam
places.notes: Founded in 1744, Giác Lâm is a historic Lâm Tế temple at 565 Lạc Long Quân, Hồ Chí Minh City. Vietnam’s National Tourism Administration identifies it as an ancestral temple of the Lâm Tế school in southern Vietnam. City reporting documents Buddhist events at the temple in 2023; no current public Zen sitting schedule was found. Describe it as an active Buddhist heritage temple with a historical Zen lineage, not as a recurring public Zen group.

places.name: Phước Hải Pagoda
places.address: 73 Mai Thị Lựu, Quận 1, HCMC
places.notes: Also known as Ngọc Hoàng (Jade Emperor) Pagoda; Lâm Tế-affiliated active temple in central HCMC.

places.name: Vĩnh Tràng Pagoda
places.address: Nguyễn Trung Trực Street, Mỹ Tho (Mỹ Phong in the tourism listing)
places.notes: The item-specific Vietnam National Authority of Tourism profile identifies Vĩnh Tràng Pagoda on Nguyễn Trung Trực Street in Mỹ Tho and its national historical-cultural relic status. The profile uses pre-2025 Tiền Giang/Mỹ Phong administrative labels; Tiền Giang was merged into Đồng Tháp in 2025 (Government of Vietnam, https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/quoc-hoi-thong-qua-nghi-quyet-sap-xep-don-vi-hanh-chinh-cap-tinh-119250612101356465.htm). Heritage/visitor evidence does not establish recurring public Zen practice. Checked 2026-10-08.
